authoredNote: Expectations written from the Svelte 5.36 declaration-tag rule (`{let x = …}` / `{const x = …}` bind a template-local for the rest of the enclosing block, exactly as `{@const}` already did) and from the grammar's own shape, probed: the pinned tree-sitter-svelte gives these NO node type — they come back as a plain `expression` whose `svelte_raw_text` is the whole `let x = …`, which is precisely why the generic mustache branch was reading the declared name. Line pins read off the post-fix run and checked against the fixture's text. The graph contract is ONE edge per `type|source|target`, so the SHADOW assertions are carried by the exact `meta.templateReadLines` arrays: `counter` is `[38]` — line 38 is ABOVE the declaration tag on line 41 and line 44 is BELOW it, so `[38]` proves both that the pre-declaration read still publishes and that the post-declaration one does not. A `line_number` forbid could not have proved either.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass. 40 declaration-tag sites in 20 of the 6,439 corpus files, producing exactly 1 false read — packages/svelte/tests/validator/samples/declaration-tag-already-declared/input.svelte, whose entire subject is that `{let foo = 'baz'}` re-declares the script's `foo`, published `uses -> foo` at the declaration line. The tag REPLACES the generic read rather than adding to it: the first version of this fix ran both, and the head was still read at line 41 — pinned here by forbidding a read at 41 while pinning the pre-declaration read at 38. Two further hazards are pinned: the RIGHT-HAND SIDE is still a read (`alpha` on 45), and the keyword needs a WORD BOUNDARY, because `{letter = 5}` is an assignment to a member named `letter` and the first version read it as `let` + binding `ter`, fabricating a shadow.

The site constraint was therefore redundant with the `line_number` this row already pins, and the pinned line was verified to equal the published one.

forbidRelationships.comment: `{const doubler = (n) => n + 1}` on 42 rebinds `doubler`; the calls on 45 and 46 are to the template-local, so only their ARGUMENTS publish. The corpus's own precedent for this half is validator/samples/declaration-tag-already-declared, where the tag's name is the script's.
`counter.value` — a member LEAF on a binding is not a component-level read

the word-boundary case: `{letter = 5}` is an ASSIGNMENT to a member named `letter`, not a `let` tag with the binding `ter`. `letter` itself IS published on 39; a fabricated `ter` shadow would also be a defect, and publishing it is the observable half.
